clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, presenting with longstanding multisystemic pigmentations, early-onset arthropathy and related musculoskeletal symptoms, as well as proteinuria and cardiovascular calcifications, was suspected for alkaptonuria. This was biochemically confirmed by positive urine homogentisic acid (HGA) spot tests in both the patient and his monozygotic twin brother. Genetic DNA testing of the twin brother further identified heterozygous pathogenic HGD gene variants c.481G>A p.(Gly161Arg) and c.1017G>T p.(Met339Ile), completing the diagnostic triad. Imaging findings included spinal cysts at Th9 and Th10 and characteristic black discoloration of bone observed intraoperatively during hip arthroplasty. These findings and the genetic/biochemical data jointly confirmed the diagnosis of alkaptonuria.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Positive urine spot test for homogentisic acid (HGA) in both brothers indicating homogentisic aciduria
Genetic DNA testing of the twin brother revealing heterozygous pathogenic variants c.481G>A p.(Gly161Arg) and c.1017G>T p.(Met339Ile) in the HGD gene
Imaging revealing spinal cysts at the corpus of Th9 and Th10 vertebrae
Intraoperative observation of distinctive black discoloration on the femur head during total hip arthroplasty
Clinical presentation with longstanding pigmentations of the auricular regions, fingers, sclera, and secondary glaucoma, along with early-onset arthropathy and osteopenia
